assigned.title: Series navigation and the next episode
assigned.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.
assigned.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict.

typecheck.evidence:
`npm run typecheck` (turbo run typecheck): Tasks 22 successful, 22 total, exit 0. Also run directly
as `npx tsc --noEmit -p apps/web/tsconfig.json`, exit 0.

`EpisodeList` became an ASYNC server component in this round and the compiler accepts it where it
is mounted -- `app/title/[titleId]/page.tsx` renders `<EpisodeList episodes={...} />` and is itself
a server component, so the async child is an ordinary RSC child rather than a promise somebody has
to await. No `any` was added; the progress index is a `ReadonlyMap<string, EpisodeProgress>` and
the card takes `EpisodeProgress | undefined`, so the absent case is in the type rather than in a
convention.

unit.evidence:
`npm run test` (turbo run test): Tasks 22 successful, 22 total, exit 0. `apps/web` alone is 81 test
files / 1417 tests passed. lint 12/12 exit 0 (one pre-existing warning in
`lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts`, not from this task).

WHAT THIS TASK'S SUITES COVER, 47 cases across three files.

`lib/next-episode.test.ts` -- 15. The pure "what plays next" rule: the ordinary case, independence
from the caller's order, the season-boundary crossing, the three absences told apart, and the
rights cases -- that an undeclared episode is never offered, that what was passed over is
REPORTED, that the href returned is the gate's own rather than one the module built, and a property
test that walks a mixed series and checks every offer against `resolvePlayAvailability`
independently.

`components/title/season-navigation.test.tsx` -- 14. The first render is the flat stack with no tab
strip, which is the property that keeps a browser without the bundle from losing four of five
seasons; a one-season series is never given a selector; and the post-hydration rules this
environment cannot execute are asserted against source with a non-vacuity check beside each --
roving tabindex, the four arrow keys, `preventDefault` only after a key has matched, panels
`hidden` rather than unmounted (so find-in-page still sees the whole series), `aria-controls`
pointing at ids the same builders produce, and the derivation that makes a stale season selection
unrepresentable rather than repaired.

`lib/episode-progress.test.ts` -- 18, new this round. The MAPPING from `continueWatchingVerdict`'s
three answers onto what an episode list says, which is where this module can be wrong in a way a
viewer sees: finished means watched; BARELY STARTED means unwatched, not in progress -- opening a
title and leaving writes a row, and a resume badge on it would re-introduce one surface over the
mistake `RESUMABLE_MINIMUM_SECONDS` exists to prevent; a lease row is unwatched; an unknown runtime
is in progress with a NULL fraction and never zero. Plus what it refuses to index (a row for a
title this page is not showing; an episode with no row stays ABSENT rather than being asserted
unwatched), that it honours the store's order for a duplicate rather than re-sorting, and the badge
copy -- including that `unknown` renders NOTHING, because a badge is a claim and a failed read has
not earned one.

EVERY THRESHOLD IS READ FROM THE EXPORTED CONSTANTS, never written as a literal:
`FINISHED_TAIL_SECONDS`, `FINISHED_FRACTION`, `RESUMABLE_MINIMUM_SECONDS` and
`CONTINUE_WATCHING_QUERY_LIMIT` are all imported from `lib/continue-watching.ts`. A test that
hardcoded 90 and 0.95 would pass after somebody changed the policy and forgot the test.

ONE EXISTING ASSERTION WAS REWRITTEN AND IT WAS LOOSENED ON PURPOSE, which is the opposite of this
repository's usual direction, so it is called out. `season-navigation.test.tsx` asserted the exact
string `<EpisodeCard episode={episode}`; adding a second prop wrapped that element onto several
lines and broke it. A test that fails because a formatter moved a newline is asserting the
formatting. It now asserts two facts instead -- `<EpisodeCard` and `episode={episode}` -- and GAINS
two: that the card is handed `progress={progress.get(episode.id)}` and that the index comes from
`loadEpisodeProgress(`. Net stricter about the property, looser about the whitespace.

VERIFIED ON A RUNNING SERVER, not only in the suite. Development build, in-memory adapter, a
profile selected, `/title/northstar`:
  before any progress ................ no badges at all
  PUT 900 of 3000 on northstar-s1e2 ... "30% watched" appears
  PUT 2990 of 3000 on northstar-s1e3 .. "Watched" appears (inside FINISHED_TAIL_SECONDS)
That read only works at all because PW-0313 landed first: before it, a server component could not
see what the progress API had written.

assigned.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
assigned.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
